roleContext.jobDescription: The transaction monitoring product at a payments company presents alert queues and case views to compliance analysts in a web application. The Web Frontend Engineer develops and maintains the alert queue and case views, owns the frontend test suites, works with the backend team on API changes, and is expected to cut the time analysts wait for the alert queue to load, reported against the product's published performance baseline.

requirements.text: Develops and maintains the alert queue and case views of the compliance web application.
Owns the component and end-to-end test suites for the application and keeps them passing in the pipeline.
Cuts alert-queue load time for analysts, reported against the published performance baseline.
Coordinates API changes with the backend team and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each application release.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Web Frontend Engineer, Transaction Monitoring

## Experience

- Developed and maintained the alert queue and case views of the compliance web application (TypeScript, Angular), including the server-side paging and column virtualisation that replaced the full-queue download.
- Owned the component test suite (Jest) and the end-to-end suite (Cypress) for the application, keeping both passing in the pipeline and adding a queue-load smoke test that gates releases.
- Median alert-queue load time for analysts fell from 6.2 seconds to 1.4 seconds after the paging release, measured by the application's real-user monitoring over the following four weeks against the published baseline of 6.2 seconds.
- Coordinated API changes with the backend team in the API review; the backend lead approved endpoint changes and I adapted the views to the paged endpoints.
- Wrote the release notes for each application release, including the known limitation that column sorting was applied per page rather than across the whole queue, and the hand-over notes for the frontend on-call.

## Work samples

- Work sample: the real-user monitoring export (median queue load time per day for eight weeks, baseline line, paging release marker) and the Cypress smoke test, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.
